newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-BIG MONEY TIME FOR WINNER HENMAN, LOSER KRAJICEK.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BIG MONEY TIME FOR WINNER HENMAN, LOSER KRAJICEK.

text.p: Britain's Tim Henman cashed in on his Wimbledon success this year by earning more than $4,000 per minute in a smooth 6-3 6-3 victory over Michael Stich at the most lucrative tournament in tennis on Tuesday.

Henman, who earned a place as a reserve at the $6 million Grand Slam Cup by reaching the Wimbledon quarter-finals and was then handed a chance to play after late withdrawals, picked up $262,500 for the first-round win.

In just 63 minutes Henman, 22, made more than twice his earnings for the whole of last year. He now has a shot at $431,250 in his quarter-final against American MaliVai Washington who destroyed Richard Krajicek 6-1 6-2 in a rematch of the Wimbledon final.
"It is nice to play in a tournament with huge amounts of money at stake. But I did not focus on the money today," said Henman.
"I am aware of it. But if you think about it you could get nervous and wouldn't be able to throw the ball up...I play tennis more as a hobby than an occupation."

The prize money at the Cup, which brings together the best performers of the year from Wimbledon and the French, U.S. and Australian Opens, was criticised for being "obscene" when the event was first set up in 1990.
Despite his defeat in just 46 minutes, Krajicek, who is due to have knee surgery next week, made more than $7,000 per minute in the defeat by Washington.
As a grand slam champion, the Dutchman was given a bonus of $250,000 for just walking out on court plus $100,000 as a first-round loser.
Australian Open champion Boris Becker also picked up the bonus and has a chance to earn much more after a 6-3 6-2 victory over Australian Jason Stoltenberg in his first match.
Henman is the first Briton to play at the Munich tournament. Stich said of his opponent: "He played very well today and is very talented. It really depends on how he deals with the attention.
"He certainly has the potential to go a long way. But there are no guarantees."

Henman deserved his victory after playing some sharp serve-and-volley tennis on the fast indoor surface. He was helped by the fact that Stich, who has been struggling with a shoulder injury, had a particularly poor day.

Henman took the initiative in the set with a break in the seventh game to lead 4-3 after Stich netted a volley. He clinched the set 6-3 after 29 minutes with another break when Stich hit a forehand out of court.
Henman, playing his first match for two weeks, then took a 3-1 lead in the second set after another break in the fourth game and never looked back.
"He made very few mistakes. He made life very difficult for me," Stich said.
Officials said Swede Thomas Enqvist had pulled out of the event with a shoulder injury. He has been replaced by Spain's Alex Corretja who plays French Open champion Yevgeny Kafelnikov on Wednesday.
